source: https://www.kaggle.com/models/metaresearch/llama-3.2 (workbook ID 139, read in Chrome 2026-10-06; Model Card tab text, no raw file saved)

modelDetails.version: Llama 3.2 1B and 3B, pretrained and instruction-tuned (text only)
modelDetails.type: Multilingual large language model (text in, text out)
modelDetails.architecture: Auto-regressive optimized transformer with grouped-query attention, 1.23B and 3.21B parameters, 128k context, shared embeddings; tuned versions use supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with human feedback
modelDetails.description: Instruction-tuned text-only models optimized for multilingual dialogue, including agentic retrieval and summarization tasks.

intendedUse.primaryIntendedUseCases: Commercial and research use in multiple languages; assistant-like chat and agentic applications such as knowledge retrieval and summarization; mobile AI-powered writing assistants; query and prompt rewriting; pretrained models can be adapted to other natural language generation tasks

factors.hardware: Meta's custom-built GPU cluster with H100-80GB GPUs (700W TDP); 830k GPU hours of training

evaluation.metrics: MMLU, AGIEval, ARC-Challenge, SQuAD, QuAC, DROP, Needle in Haystack, IFEval, GSM8K, MATH, GPQA, Hellaswag, BFCL V2, Nexus, InfiniteBench, MGSM and multilingual MMLU
evaluation.datasets: Standard automatic benchmarks run with Meta's internal evaluations library; dedicated adversarial evaluation datasets for safety
evaluation.performance: Instruction-tuned 3B: MMLU 63.4, IFEval 77.4, GSM8K 77.7, MATH 47.3, ARC-C 78.6; instruction-tuned 1B: MMLU 49.3, IFEval 59.5, GSM8K 44.4

trainingData.algorithm: Auto-regressive optimized transformer; supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning with human feedback
trainingData.dataset: Up to 9 trillion tokens of publicly available online data with a cutoff of December 2023, plus logits from Llama 3.1 8B and 70B
trainingData.procedure: Pretraining with logits from Llama 3.1 8B and 70B as token-level targets, pruning and knowledge distillation, then several rounds of supervised fine-tuning, rejection sampling and direct preference optimization

ethicalConsiderations.typeOfBias: The model may in some instances produce inaccurate, biased or other objectionable responses
ethicalConsiderations.riskFactors: Testing has not covered all scenarios and outputs cannot be predicted in advance; critical risk areas are chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear and explosive weapons, child safety and cyber attacks; small models in constrained environments have a different safety and helpfulness tradeoff
ethicalConsiderations.riskMitigation: Recurring red teaming exercises whose findings improve benchmarks and safety tuning datasets; an output reporting mechanism and a bug bounty program
ethicalConsiderations.safetyMeasures: Safety fine-tuning with human-generated and synthetic data, LLM-based classifiers to select prompts and responses, refusal and tone tuning, and safeguards provided to the community (Llama Guard, Prompt Guard and Code Shield)
ethicalConsiderations.safetyAndSecurityPolicy: Developed following the Responsible Use Guide; use is subject to the Acceptable Use Policy
ethicalConsiderations.misuseCases: Use in any manner that violates applicable laws or regulations (including trade compliance laws); use prohibited by the Acceptable Use Policy and the Llama 3.2 Community License; use in languages beyond those explicitly supported
ethicalConsiderations.limitations: Static model trained on an offline dataset; only English, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, Hindi, Spanish and Thai are officially supported; testing has not covered all scenarios

modelCardContent.caveatsAndRecommendations: Developers should perform safety testing and tuning tailored to their application before deployment; deploy the model as part of an overall AI system with additional safeguards; use lighter system safeguards such as Llama Guard 3-1B in constrained environments; evaluate applications in context with a dedicated evaluation dataset; comply with the Llama 3.2 Community License and the Acceptable Use Policy when fine-tuning for other languages
